teaser: A page-by-page tour of the Mesa Ranch observation vault: the argument, the system, the record, five graphs, and how to open and rebuild it.
core_idea: The Mesa Ranch observation desk turns Marconi's INMA deck into seventeen vault pages on synthetic records, all in one frame of menu, page and details panel; the tour explains each page, what to click and what it proves, from delta science and the atlas of 78 event types to the fractal semantic graph and the knowledge graph played in time, and ends with how to open, clone and rebuild it for another beat.

figures.caption: The vault's cover page: the menu on the left groups the seventeen pages as the deck does, the synthetic campus is drawn in pen and ink with orange markers, and the panel on the right waits for anything you click.

Journalism is delta science, after: the same landscape with a permitted power station, three data halls and four documents, Permissions, Resources, Ownership and Commitments, each opening its record in the panel.

An atlas of events: twelve families around the buildout, each with its featured event and how many of its types have been seen; Power and utilities is open in the panel, with every event type's definition and observable signal.

A domain ontology: campus, building, construction work, source record, company and project, with the six relationships between them; click an entity to see what it relates to and the observations that changed it.

Every observation adds to what the newsroom knows: four headline folders, from the air permit in January to the power target in September, and the full history below; the selected observation, its comparison and its records are in the panel.

The AI workflow, stepped through one cycle: observe, compare, check, report and update, with a small graph that grows at each step, from the investor presentation to the alert and the updated history.
The community impact tracker: jobs, water, power, land and public commitments, each item a claim, a change or an open question with its record; beside it, the draft article and the two alerts.
The fractal semantic graph at level 1: the campus opens into the twelve event families; the number on each node is how many more it opens into, and the breadcrumb leads back to the question.
Every level at once: the question at the centre, then the twelve families, the 78 event types, the observations and the records in rings, with evidence in orange.

The knowledge graph, in time: the campus, its buildings, the projects, the companies, the county, the water district and the residents, played one observation at a time; at the acquisition, the new relationship is orange.

Records to observations: sixteen synthetic records on the left, seventeen observations on the right, and the evidence between them; the solid line is each observation's main record, the dashed ones the other records it cites.
The delta chain: observations on a time axis, by the entity they change, with an arc from each to the earlier observation it was compared with, and the comparisons listed below.
